the ectD gene encodes a non-heme-iron-dependent dioxygenase, which catalyzes the stereospecific hydroxyl group insertion at C-5 in ectoine to yield 5-hydroxymethyl-4,5-dihydro-2(5H)-furanone.

the hydroxylation of ectoines is a widespread phenomenon that is found in a large number of microorganisms and that the ectoine hydroxylation reaction is an important step in the synthesis of the compatible solute 5-hydroxymethyl-ectoine.
the ectoine hydroxylation reaction is widespread among microorganisms, and that the ectoine biosynthesis gene cluster is highly conserved in the genomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified the EctD enzymes from six different microorganisms and characterized them in detail.

the ectoine and hydroxylases are widespread among Bacteria, that their genes are organized in a conserved operon, that the hydroxyectoine synthesis genes are frequently found adjacent to the gene encoding the aspartokinase, and that the EctD enzymes from different species exhibit similar catalytic properties but differ in their thermal stability and salt tolerance.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the EctD enzymes are not only present in the halophilic and alkalophilic bacteria that produce hydroxy ectoine, but also in a variety of other microorganisms that produce ectoine only.
ectoine hydroxylation is not restricted to extremophilic bacteria and that ectoine hydroxylation may be a common feature in the physiology of many bacteria.
